preamble: Fronting and unrounding of /o/ to /e/. In Latin, the sequence vo- became ve- before s, t and r plus consonant during the 2nd century BC, so that Plautine vortō, voster and vortex gave Classical vertō 'turn', vester 'your' and vertex.

examples.note: Part of the 2nd-century BC change vo- > ve- before s, t and r plus consonant.
The older vo- form survived in Vulgar Latin and underlies Spanish vuestro and Italian vostro.
The two forms survived side by side as doublets.
